document_summary: A long devotional zikr led almost entirely by Rashad on the Night of Destiny. He compares remembrance with rapid growth of the soul from infancy to adolescence and calls it the most nourishing form of worship. Participants repeatedly recite 'there is no god except God,' God's name, Qayyum, Subhan Allah, alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar. Quran 20:14 is used to say Contact Prayer exists to commemorate God alone. The group chants a community 'national anthem,' recites al-Fatihah, and begins a second zikr cycle tied to Sura al-Qadr. Rashad says angels descend that night to execute every command and may recognize participants' dearest wishes. The closing chants connect body and soul with the premortal covenant, describe each remembrance as an enormous deposit in a post-retirement account, and promise health, wealth, dignity, and perfect happiness under God's law.

sections.title: Zikr as accelerated growth and nourishment for the soul
sections.summary: Rashad says the group's spiritual growth through zikr resembles a baby rapidly becoming a teenager. He calls remembrance God's most beloved form of worship and compares it with a steak-and-lobster meal for the soul. Participants are instructed to concentrate until the words become the dominant thought and every cell seems to repeat them.
